header.title: Structural global rearmament supercycle lifts defense primes' multi-year revenue visibility

s01_bottom_line.text: Record and growing global defense budgets ($2.89tn in 2025, US FY2027 request of $1.5tn) are feeding historically large order books, with Lockheed Martin at a record $230bn backlog and Rheinmetall guiding toward ~$151bn, giving established manufacturers multiyear revenue visibility. ⟨cited figures: forecast; approximate⟩
The article argues the strongest opportunities capture a 'readiness premium' and advises investors to distinguish funded programs from announcements and repeat orders from pilots.

The scale and persistence of government spending plus surging backlogs point to durable top-line growth for defense primes, but the article does not quantify earnings or valuation impact, and warns a larger market won't reward every entrant.
